blocks.text: This article provides a summary of all new features and enhancements for DSPM. To see scheduled maintenance updates for your cloud, visit the Trust Portal.

blocks.heading: Apply MIP Labels to Multiple Files in Resource Inventory

blocks.text: You can now manually apply Microsoft Purview Information Protection (MIP) labels to multiple files in the on-premises file shares on the Resource Inventory page. This allows you to classify and protect files containing sensitive data.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the Sensitive Data Details.
DSPM investigates the service principal metadata and discovers Azure applications and categorizes them as:
This information is displayed in the Resource Inventory graph, giving you visibility into the Azure applications that have access to resources and data in your environment.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the Graph for Azure Data Stores.
The Compliance dashboard includes the following enhancements:

blocks.item: A new tab, Findings, is available listing the open issues for specific resources and for the selected compliance framework.

The Saved View option is available for all the tabs. You can apply filters, show or hide columns in the table, and save this page setting. This allows you to return to the same customized page view without having to reapply the settings each time you visit the page.

The Data Stores column on the Policies tab is clickable. Clicking the number of data stores redirects you to the Findings tab to view the resources that are noncompliant, along with the policy ID pre-selected.

blocks.text: To learn more, see Viewing Compliance Details.

DSPM now supports the onboarding of Google Cloud Platform (GCP) single projects to monitor and scan the data stores within them. This option can be used when there are restrictions for onboarding projects at the organization level.
See image.
To learn more, see Onboarding a GCP Project.

ZAgent is powered by agentic AI to enhance the capabilities of the AI virtual assistant that is dedicated to troubleshooting multistep tasks and answering complex questions. You can select the predefined Data Protection as an agent to jumpstart your AI workflow to access Zscaler's knowledge base or analyze data to understand the data protection of your organization's multi-cloud platforms.
See image.
To learn more, see About ZAgent and Understanding ZAgent with Use Cases.

DSPM now supports the onboarding of Azure single subscriptions to monitor and scan the data stores within them. This option can be used when there are restrictions for onboarding subscriptions at the tenant or management group level.
See image.
To learn more, see Onboarding an Azure Subscription.

blocks.heading: Manual File Actions in Data Inventory

blocks.text: You can now manually apply Microsoft Purview Information Protection (MIP) labels to single or multiple on-premises file shares created on file servers and Azure file shares. This allows you to review and remediate files containing sensitive data. Users with the Actions Apply Label permission can apply the labels.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the Data Inventory.

The SaaS Overview dashboard is now moved under DSPM. The SaaS Overview dashboard visually displays the detected incidents, showing their distribution and identifying affected applications and users. You can view the total number of SaaS incidents, list of user accounts with the most number of SaaS incidents, and SaaS applications containing sensitive data that are publicly exposed to the internet. This information allows you to identify the overall security risk and prioritize mitigation based on the incident type and affected entities.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the SaaS Overview Dashboard.

blocks.heading: Saved Views in Alerts and Data Duplications

blocks.text: The Saved Views option is available for Alerts and Data Duplications. You can apply filters, show or hide columns in the table, and save this page setting. This allows you to return to the same customized page view without having to reapply the settings each time you visit the page.
See image.
To learn more, see About Alerts and About Data Duplications.
The graph for Snowflake database includes a public internet node that provides visibility of databases that are publicly exposed to the internet.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the Graph for Databases.

The Data Duplications Report and the Data Duplications tab display files detected in SaaS services for subscriptions that include both DSPM and out-of-the-box (OOB) CASB. You can review identical files across cloud services, on-premises file shares, and SaaS services such as M365, JIRA, Google Drive, and Salesforce.
See image.
To learn more, see About Data Duplications.

blocks.text: The Identity Inventory is now more intuitive with clearer, human-readable entity information, new ways to view and filter identities by category, source, and cloud service providers. These improvements are also available in the Access tab on the Resource Inventory page.
The Identity Inventory includes the following new columns:

blocks.item: Entity Source: The repository (e.g., AWS Cloud Resource, EntraID) where the identity data is stored.
Entity Category: The entity category (e.g., External users, Services).
Target Environment: The cloud service providers (e.g., GCP) that the identity can access.

blocks.text: See image.
To learn more, see About Identity Inventory and Viewing the Access Levels.

blocks.heading: Saved Views in the Data Inventory and Resource Inventory

blocks.text: Saved Views functionality is available for the Data Inventory and Resource Inventory. You can apply filters, show or hide columns in the table, and save this page setting. This allows you to return to the same customized view without having to reapply the settings each time you visit the page.
See image.
To learn more, see About Resource Inventory and Viewing the Data Inventory.

blocks.heading: Support for Selecting DLP Engines to Scan Data

blocks.text: Zscaler DLP engines are configured centrally and used for DLP classification engines across channels such as web, email, DSPM, endpoints, and SaaS Security. You can now select specific DLP engines for DSPM and reduce the extra noise from other DLP engines applied to other channels.
All existing DLP engines are assigned to DSPM by default. You can enable or disable the DSPM channel in the Zscaler Admin Console.
See image.
To learn more, see Understanding DLP Engines and Dictionaries and Editing Predefined DLP Engines.

Links are added to the Top Sensitive Data At Rest section in the Unified dashboard. This allows you to investigate the relevant files and database tables. For data stored in public cloud and on-premises environments, these links navigate to the Data Inventory.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the Data Security Dashboard.
Data Inventory includes the following enhancements:

blocks.heading: SaaS Data in the Data Inventory

blocks.text: Zscaler has now unified data-at-rest findings under DSPM, bringing together cloud, on-premises, and SaaS data into the same reports and workflows. Customers subscribed to Out-of-Band CASB can view the SaaS data findings within the Data Inventory report. This allows you to explore sensitive data findings in files stored on clouds, on-premises, and SaaS applications in a single report.
See image.

blocks.heading: Entitlement Findings in On-Premises SMB File Shares

blocks.text: DSPM provides support to scan the on-premises SMB file shares and detect identities (users, groups, and computer accounts) that have access to sensitive data. This allows you to review and restrict specific identities from accessing sensitive data.
See image.
To enable this scan, you must register a Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) server and associate it with your on-premises file servers.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the Data Inventory, Adding an LDAP Server, and Adding an On-Premises File Server.

blocks.text: Data scanning includes the following enhancements:

blocks.heading: Exclude VM Folders or Directories from Scanning

blocks.text: You can now choose to exclude specific operating system directories or non-critical folders on a VM from scans by specifying the file and directory paths while configuring the scan rules.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Scan Rule for AWS Virtual Machines, Configuring Scan Rule for GCP Virtual Machines, and Configuring Scan Rule for Azure Virtual Machines.
While configuring scan rules for Databricks, you can select specific catalogs within a workspace for more granular control by limiting the discovery and classification of specific data.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Scan Rule for AWS Databricks and Configuring Scan Rule for Azure Databricks.
DSPM supports evidence collection for on-premises sensitive data. Evidence snippets discovered while scanning on-premises data are stored in a customer-managed cloud storage.
See image.
To learn more, see About Evidence Settings and Adding an Evidence Rule.

DSPM provides support for Kerberos authentication for scanning NetApp Network File System (NFS) and Server Message Block (SMB) file shares, providing a more secure authentication method for NetApp environments.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding an On-Premises File Server.

DSPM now supports only custom network configuration for onboarding cloud accounts, where you must set up the network by creating virtual networks (VNets) or virtual private clouds (VPCs) in the orchestrator account.
The default network configuration using Zscaler-managed resources is removed.
To learn more, see:
The Data Classification Settings page includes the following enhancements:

blocks.item: The Data Sensitivity Settings page is renamed to Data Classification Settings.
You can select the DLP engines DSPM uses for data classification and specify which of the enabled DLP engines must be used to identify sensitive data for alerting purposes.
DSPM provides a set of predefined DLP engines built with high accuracy for data classification.

blocks.text: See image.
To learn more, see About Data Classification Settings.

File path is clickable, providing quick access to file details.
Clicking the number of copies directs you to the Duplications tab for detailed analysis.

blocks.text: See image.

Click the icon next to the file path to access the original file in the third-party console.
Data store links direct you to the Risk Explorer tab in the Resource Inventory page.

blocks.text: See image.
To learn more, see About Data Duplications.
The detailed view for files related to the Data Inventory is displayed in the following tabs:
The tabs are visible based on the assigned permissions.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the Data Inventory.

blocks.text: Data scanning includes the following enhancements:

When performing a data sampling scan on Relational Database Management Systems (RDBMS), random rows are selected from each table. This provides a more accurate representation of data, reduces scan times and less impact on large databases.
To learn more, see About Scan Settings.

DSPM provides 70 predefined data classification engines for common sensitive data types, such as credit cards, Social Security numbers (SSNs), national IDs, and driver's licenses. These engines are built with high accuracy and help reduce false positives. You can select the engines while configuring the scan scope.
To learn more, see Understanding Data Classification and About Data Sensitivity Settings.

DSPM is now available in Experience Center, a centralized unified platform that provides a more secure and streamlined user experience. You can access and manage DSPM in the Zscaler Admin Console for Experience Center.
See image.
To learn more, see What is Zscaler Experience Center? and Upgrading to Zscaler Experience Center.

You can now use only on-premises scanners to scan on-premises databases. DSPM no longer provides support for using cloud scanners to scan on-premises databases. While registering an unmanaged database, you can only select an on-premises scanner.
See image.
To learn more, see About On-Premises Data Centers, Managing an On-Premises Data Center, Adding Unmanaged Databases, and Editing or Deleting Unmanaged Databases.
The Resource Inventory includes the following enhancements:

blocks.heading: File Details in Sensitive Data Tab

blocks.text: The file details are shown in the following tabs:
The tabs are visible based on the assigned permissions.
See image.
You can use CSV templates to register and onboard multiple unmanaged database servers at once instead of onboarding individual databases at a time.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding Unmanaged Databases and About Service Registration.

You can test the connectivity between DSPM and registered services, such as unmanaged databases, Snowflake, and Databricks, before initiating a scan. This allows you to verify the network connectivity, credentials, secret, and basic service access.
See image.
To learn more, see About Service Registration, Adding Unmanaged Databases, Adding a Snowflake Database Account, and Adding a Databricks Workspace or Account.
DSPM generates evidence data for scanned files and tables which allows in-context investigation and validation of sensitive data. This is now supported for Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
To learn more, see:
The export feature on the Data Duplications page includes two new options:

blocks.item: Summary View: This report provides the total number of duplicate files including their locations across accounts and regions.

Full View: This report provides the complete list of all duplicate file instances and their attributes, allowing you to identify the exact location of every file to ensure no redundant data is missed during remediation.

blocks.text: See image.
To learn more, see Viewing Duplicate Files.

blocks.text: Data scanning includes the following enhancements:

blocks.heading: Support for On-Premises NetApp File Shares

blocks.text: DSPM supports the discovery and classification of sensitive data in on-premises NetApp file shares using NFS and SMB protocols.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding an On-Premises File Server.
DSPM provides visibility into all columns that contain sensitive data, precisely matching the data types with the specific columns in the database table.
You can view the results of column-level scanning on:

blocks.item: Data Tab: View column-level sensitive data classifications and the associated DLP dictionaries.
Column-Specific Evidence Tab: View the evidence details based on the column-level scanning, organized by column and DLP dictionary for detailed investigation.

blocks.text: DSPM supports Optical Character Recognition (OCR) scanning to scan and identify sensitive data in images embedded in files (PDF, Word, PPT, etc.).
To learn more, see Viewing the Sensitive Data Details and Viewing the Data Inventory.

blocks.heading: Discovery Status and Error Messages for On-Premises File Servers

blocks.text: You can now view detailed error messages when on-premises file servers cannot be discovered for scanning. The error message includes specific reasons for failure, such as networking, authentication, or permission issues, to resolve the issues.
See image.
To learn more, see About Service Registration.

DSPM supports onboarding of Microsoft 365 (M365) tenants to monitor and scan data stores, access Microsoft Information Protection (MIP) labels for Microsoft Azure or on-premises file shares, or integrate with Microsoft Copilot.
See image.
To learn more, see:
The following enhancements are included:

blocks.heading: MIP Labeling for On-Premises File Shares

blocks.text: DSPM extends Microsoft Information Protection (MIP) labeling for on-premises SMB and NFS file shares. Use action rules to automatically apply MIP sensitivity labels to sensitive data (e.g., PII, PHI, PCI).
See image.
To learn more, see About Action Rules and Adding Action Rules.

You can view the activities related to applying MIP labeling on the File Activity tab. You can see what action was performed (e.g., Apply Label), the entity that performed the action (e.g., Zscaler), and the timestamp.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the Sensitive Data Details and Viewing the Data Inventory.

Action rules allow you to define the criteria for identifying specific data types and to automatically apply Microsoft Information Protection sensitivity labels to files. This feature currently supports Azure File Shares
See image.
To learn more, see About Action Rules.
The following threat categories are available to assess AI governance and safety:
See image.
To learn more, see Understanding Threat Categories.
DSPM AI security includes the following enhancements:

DSPM scans AI models to identify vulnerabilities such as malicious code injection, backdoors, embedded secrets, data leakage, etc. The scan results are displayed on the AI Model Security Scan Findings page.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing Scan Results for AI Models, About Scanning AI Models, Deploying the AI Model Scanner, and Managing AI Model Scan Integrations.

blocks.heading: Scanning AWS ECR Images for Vulnerabilities

blocks.text: DSPM provides support to scan AWS ECR images, and provides visibility into model usage, licensing, versions, and security vulnerabilities across containerized machine learning workloads.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Scan Rule for AWS ECR Images.
DSPM provides visibility into deployed Azure AI Agents and the sensitive data they have access to.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing Services.

blocks.heading: Visibility into Google Cloud Vertex AI

blocks.text: DSPM supports the discovery of GCP Vertex AI and its access to sensitive data, as well as determining entitlement and posture.
To learn more, see Onboarding a GCP Organization.

blocks.heading: CLI Command to Initialize Scanner VM

blocks.text: A new CLI command is available to initialize the on-premises scanner. This helps simplify the network configuration and allows you to configure the scanner, install required components, and run initial connectivity and health checks.
To learn more, see Initializing the On-Premises Scanner VM.
